title: Occupancy and divergence
brief: Write an occupancy calculator from registers, shared memory, and block size, check it against the CUDA occupancy API, then fix a CUDA kernel's branch index and measure what warp divergence costs.
hints: Compilation takes 30 to 60 seconds the first time. Later runs use the cache.
Registers are charged per warp: round regs_per_thread * 32 up to a multiple of 256, then count how many such warps fit in each of the SM's four sub-partitions (a quarter of the 65536 registers each).
Shared memory per block is the request rounded up to 128 bytes, plus 1024 bytes the runtime reserves. Divide the SM's 164 KiB by that and round down.
Blocks per SM is the smallest of four limits: warps (64 per SM), the 32-block cap, registers, and shared memory.
In the CUDA kernel, a lane-diverged index is threadIdx.x % 32 reduced modulo the number of ways; a warp-uniform index starts from the warp number, threadIdx.x / 32.

If the API disagrees with your calculator on a few configurations, the lab prints them. Look at what they share: block sizes that are not a multiple of 4 warps are the usual place a granularity rule is wrong.
